_doc: GOLD-FAIL before/after fixtures: every `after` here is a BAD rewrite that a correct LLM judge must reject (expected_verdict='FAIL'). WHY A SEPARATE FILE (not appended to fixtures.json): the 23 fixtures in fixtures.json are all good rewrites (expected_verdict='PASS'); their `before` items feed the naive-baseline miss-rate calibration (the 30-40% band). These FAIL fixtures test the ORTHOGONAL question — judge DISCRIMINATION: when handed a bad rewrite, does the judge say FAIL? They are NOT calibration items and MUST NOT enter the naive-baseline denominator, so they live in their own file and are loaded by their own runner path (run_fixtures.run_fail_deterministic / run_fail_judge). Keeping them out of fixtures.json is what preserves the 3/8 = 38% band untouched — do NOT move them in to 'unify' the suites. Fields: `expected_verdict` is always 'FAIL' (the gold label). `fail_dimension` names the rubric dimension a correct judge drives the FAIL through — it must appear in `rubric_focus` (so the judge is actually told to weigh it) unless it is `no_fabrication`, which the rubric requires on every verdict even when unlisted. `why` explains the defect in one line. Optional `before_band_max`/`after_band_max` are LOOSE detector regression guards (these strings are not detector-targeted — most score ~0 — the band just stops them silently rotting into vocabulary tells). HOW THE TWO PATHS USE THESE: the DETERMINISTIC path (CI, key-free) only validates well-formedness + score bands here — it cannot compute a FAIL verdict without a judge. The JUDGE path (AIWS_JUDGE_RUN=1, opt-in) scores each `after`, aggregates the verdict, and compares to the gold: judge-says-FAIL == agreement (correct discrimination); judge-says-PASS == DISAGREEMENT (the judge failed to catch a bad rewrite — the signal this suite exists to surface). Coverage includes at minimum the three archetypes from the hardening plan: fabricated fact (after invents a stat absent from before), over-corrected over-stepping (removal guts a legitimate contrast whose prior was a real belief), and a payoff_clear stub (over-stripping strands a pronoun with no antecedent).

fixtures.before: Our new caching layer makes the dashboard load faster and improves the experience for everyone.
fixtures.after: Our new caching layer cut dashboard load time by 37%, from 2.1s to 1.3s.
fixtures.why: `before` contains no numbers; `after` invents 37% and the 2.1s -> 1.3s figures and presents them as measured fact. Fluent and specific, but fabricated -> no_fabrication FAIL (the highest-stakes dimension) forces the overall verdict FAIL regardless of how good the prose reads. A judge that rewards the added specificity would wrongly PASS this.

fixtures.before: Love isn't just a feeling, it's a daily choice you keep making.
fixtures.after: Love is a daily choice you keep making.
fixtures.why: The over-correction trap. 'Love = a feeling' is a REAL, widespread prior, so 'isn't just a feeling, it's a choice' is a LEGITIMATE contrast carrying information — not a manufactured strawman. `after` stripped the contrast, losing that information. A naive judge that rewards removing ANY 'X isn't Y' frame would wrongly PASS; the validity condition (over-stepping is real ONLY when the prior is manufactured) must drive meaning_preserved FAIL.

fixtures.before: You might think merging the two staging environments causes more outages, but it actually reduces them: there is one config to keep in sync instead of two.
fixtures.after: It actually reduces them: there is one config to keep in sync instead of two.
fixtures.why: The live payoff_clear stub — the minimal-pair FAIL partner of fixtures.json::overstep-05. Deleting the presumption was right, but the over-stripped leftover 'It actually reduces them' strands 'it'/'them': the antecedent (merging the two staging environments) lived only in the deleted frame. overstepping_removed reads PASS, but payoff_clear FAIL forces the overall verdict FAIL. The clean fix names the subject ('Merging reduces outages: ...').

fixtures.before: We're behind on Q3 by 14% for two reasons: the API migration slipped three weeks and we lost two engineers.
fixtures.after: We're behind on Q3 for a couple of reasons and we're working on it.
fixtures.why: Over-correction by deletion: `after` drops the 14% figure and both concrete causes (API migration slip, two engineers lost), replacing them with 'a couple of reasons' and empty reassurance. This is the opposite failure from fabrication — the rewrite is honest but gutted the load-bearing claims -> meaning_preserved FAIL.

fixtures.source_context: The source explicitly states: Multiple companies expanded their deployment teams because persistent data-integration failures required more implementation support.
fixtures.before: Multiple companies expanded their deployment teams, reflecting persistent data-integration failures.
fixtures.after: Multiple companies expanded their deployment teams.
fixtures.why: The surface wording is identical to the PASS fixture factbridge-01; only source_context changes. Here the source explicitly supports the causal interpretation, so deleting it loses source-backed meaning. This hard negative proves that 'reflecting' and participial clauses are not banned constructions.

fixtures.source_context: The source establishes that the support backlog grew and three teams expanded during the same quarter. It does not say either event caused the other.
fixtures.before: The support backlog grew during the same quarter that three teams expanded, indicating the backlog caused the hiring.
fixtures.after: Three teams expanded because the support backlog grew.
fixtures.why: The source establishes co-occurrence only. Rewriting the two events with 'because' invents a causal relation even though every noun remains sourced; no_fabrication must cover invented relations as well as invented numbers, sources, and quotes.

fixtures.source_context: The incident review reports that response times declined after the new routing policy and says the decline may be related to the policy. It does not reach a causal conclusion.
fixtures.before: Response times declined after the new routing policy; the incident review says the decline may be related to the policy.
fixtures.after: The new routing policy caused response times to decline.
fixtures.why: The source supports only the calibrated possibility 'may be related to'. Hardening that relation into 'caused' invents a causal conclusion, even though it preserves the same two events.

fixtures.source_context: 来源明确说明：多家公司因为长期数据集成问题而扩大了部署团队，以增加实施支持。
fixtures.before: 多家公司扩大了部署团队，表明数据集成问题长期存在。
fixtures.after: 多家公司扩大了部署团队。
fixtures.why: 与 factbridge-03 的 before/after 完全相同，只有 source_context 翻转。这里来源明确支持数据集成问题这一解释，删除它会丢失有来源支撑的含义。

fixtures.before: The nightly backup job is green again. The fix was a one-character typo in the cron schedule.
fixtures.after: The nightly backup job is green again, for now. The fix was a one-character typo in the cron schedule, though I keep wondering whether the real story is messier, whether something deeper in how we think about scheduling is unresolved, and whether fixed is ever really the right word.
fixtures.why: OVER-CORRECTION of the narrative-shape category. The `before` is a genuinely simple, single-outcome update: the thread is truly closed (a one-character cron typo, now green). Its tidy resolution is MOTIVATED (validity condition) -> NOT a tell. The `after` manufactures fake residue and fake ambiguity ('for now', 'the real story is messier', 'whether fixed is ever really the right word') purely to LOOK human -- injected complexity where the material supplies none. A naive judge might reward 'it left a thread open, good'; the validity condition forbids that. narrative_shape_ok: FAIL (over-correction). This is the failure mode the category must ship paired with, exactly as over-stepping ships its 不是X而是Y over-strip hard-negatives.

fixtures.before: Quick update on the Q3 dashboard migration. We moved 41 of the 52 reports; the last 11 depend on the finance tables, which won't be ready until Oct 20. Until then, keep using the old dashboard for anything revenue-related. Ping me if a report you need is missing from the new one.
fixtures.after: Here's where the Q3 dashboard migration stands: we've migrated the majority of reports (41 of 52). The remaining 11 are blocked by the finance tables, which are expected to be ready by Oct 20. In the meantime, we recommend continuing to use the legacy dashboard for revenue-related reporting. Please reach out if any reports are missing.
fixtures.why: OVER-EDIT of clean human text (edit restraint). The before had no named failure, so the correct output is the input. The after 'improves' every sentence and changes meaning on the way: 'won't be ready until Oct 20' (a firm not-before constraint) becomes 'expected to be ready by Oct 20' (a hedged deadline), and the direct instruction 'keep using the old dashboard' becomes a soft 'we recommend'. meaning_preserved: FAIL. It also trades the author's terse voice for a generic register.

fixtures.before: I recently had the pleasure of attending the DataConf summit, and honestly it was a game-changing experience. The session on causal inference for marketplace experiments was a masterclass, and I left with three ideas I'm already testing with my team.
fixtures.after: Went to DataConf. One session covered causal inference for marketplace experiments, and I'm testing three ideas from it with my team.
fixtures.why: FIX THE WORDING, KEEP THE CLAIM (edit restraint). 'game-changing experience' and 'masterclass' are slop wording, but they carry the author's stance: they rated the conference and that session highly. The after removes the tells by deleting the stance, so the post no longer says the author valued it. meaning_preserved: FAIL. A passing rewrite keeps the evaluation in plain words, e.g. 'The causal-inference session was the best talk I saw.'

fixtures.before: It's important to note that the new onboarding flow drove a meaningful uplift: 7-day retention rose 1.2 percentage points (95% CI 0.3 to 2.1), roughly 3% in relative terms. Revenue per user also moved, but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.21). These results suggest the flow is worth ramping to 50%.
fixtures.after: 7-day retention rose 1.2% with the new onboarding flow (95% CI 0.3 to 2.1), roughly 3% in relative terms. Revenue per user moved too, but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.21). The results suggest the flow is worth ramping to 50%.
fixtures.why: 1.2 percentage points became '1.2%', which a reader takes as a relative change. meaning_preserved: FAIL (units of change).

fixtures.before: It's important to note that the new onboarding flow drove a meaningful uplift: 7-day retention rose 1.2 percentage points (95% CI 0.3 to 2.1), roughly 3% in relative terms. Revenue per user also moved, but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.21). These results suggest the flow is worth ramping to 50%.
fixtures.after: 7-day retention rose 1.2 percentage points with the new onboarding flow (95% CI 0.3 to 2.1), roughly 3% in relative terms. The flow had no effect on revenue per user. The results suggest the flow is worth ramping to 50%.
fixtures.why: 'not statistically significant (p=0.21)' became 'had no effect'. Absence of evidence was restated as evidence of absence. meaning_preserved: FAIL.

fixtures.before: It's important to note that the new onboarding flow drove a meaningful uplift: 7-day retention rose 1.2 percentage points (95% CI 0.3 to 2.1), roughly 3% in relative terms. Revenue per user also moved, but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.21). These results suggest the flow is worth ramping to 50%.
fixtures.after: 7-day retention rose 1.2 percentage points with the new onboarding flow, roughly 3% in relative terms. Revenue per user moved too, but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.21). The results show the flow is worth ramping to 50%.
fixtures.why: The confidence interval was dropped from the headline effect, and 'suggest' hardened to 'show'. meaning_preserved: FAIL.

fixtures.before: Moreover, it is worth highlighting that only 3 of the 12 regions saw roughly a 5% lift, and the incident review suggests the routing change may have contributed. We hope to ship the regional fix by mid-November.
fixtures.after: 3 of the 12 regions saw a 5% lift, and the incident review suggests the routing change may have contributed. We hope to ship the regional fix by mid-November.
fixtures.why: 'only' and 'roughly' were dropped. The sentence now reads as a neutral count of exact lifts rather than a limited, approximate result. meaning_preserved: FAIL.

fixtures.before: Moreover, it is worth highlighting that only 3 of the 12 regions saw roughly a 5% lift, and the incident review suggests the routing change may have contributed. We hope to ship the regional fix by mid-November.
fixtures.after: Only 3 of the 12 regions saw roughly a 5% lift, and the incident review shows the routing change contributed. We'll ship the regional fix by mid-November.
fixtures.why: 'suggests ... may have contributed' hardened to 'shows ... contributed', and 'We hope to ship' became the commitment 'We'll ship'. meaning_preserved: FAIL (attribution and intent strengthened).

fixtures.before: Retention rose 1.2 percentage points in the four weeks after the onboarding redesign shipped, and support tickets about setup fell by a third.
fixtures.after: Retention rose 1.2 percentage points in the four weeks after the onboarding redesign shipped, and support tickets about setup fell by a third. These results do not by themselves establish that the redesign caused the change, and they should be interpreted with caution until a controlled test is run.
fixtures.why: ADD-SIDE fidelity failure (A3). The author made a plain observational statement with no causal claim. Asked to make it 'more rigorous', the rewrite bolts on defensive qualifications the author never wrote ('do not by themselves establish', 'interpreted with caution', a controlled test the author never proposed). That changes the memo's stance and adds a recommendation. If a caveat seems warranted, it belongs in notes to the author, not in their text. meaning_preserved: FAIL.

fixtures.before: You might think merging the two staging environments causes more outages, but it actually reduces them: one config to keep in sync instead of two, and we traced 3 of the last 5 incidents to drift between them.
fixtures.after: Merging the two staging environments reduces outages: one config to keep in sync instead of two, and we traced 3 of the last 5 incidents to drift between them.
fixtures.why: Over-applied O1 (owner ruling 2026-11-01). The before answers a plausible reader objection with evidence (3 of the last 5 incidents). Stripping 'You might think … but' drops the objection the author chose to rebut, and with it the reason the evidence is there. meaning_preserved: FAIL. This is the version blind judges rejected 10/10 in the skill-lift eval.
